front: In Amazon S3, S3 encrypts the data at rest, but the company keeps the encryption keys outside AWS. Which option fits?
extra: With SSE-C, S3 encrypts and decrypts the data, and [you retain control of the encryption keys](../facts/s3.md#s3-faq-sse-c-keys). [Starting April 2026](../facts/s3.md#s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04), [SSE-C is disabled by default](../facts/s3.md#s3-sse-c-disabled-by-default-2026-04) on new buckets, so you turn it on first.

front: In Amazon S3, can a lifecycle rule move an object from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval back to S3 Standard?
back: No. Restore it, then copy it.
extra: Lifecycle transitions follow [a waterfall model for transitioning between storage classes](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-transition-waterfall), toward colder classes. To change the class of an archived object, [make a temporary copy of the object first](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-no-transition-out-of-archive), then copy it with the new class.

front: In Amazon S3, an Expedited retrieval of a smaller object from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval typically takes {{c1::1–5 minutes}}.
